name: Champs-Élysées to Notre-Dame
blurb: From the Arc de Triomphe along the Seine, with nowhere to be.

texts: The Arc de Triomphe was ordered by Napoleon in 1806, and took thirty years to finish.
Beneath the Arc de Triomphe lies the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier, whose flame is rekindled every evening.
Twelve avenues meet at the Arc de Triomphe, which is why the square around it was called the Star.
The big fight in John Wick Chapter Four, from 2023, is set in the traffic around the Arc de Triomphe. The crew had only a few hours at the real arch, so much of it was filmed elsewhere.
Every fourteenth of July, the Bastille Day military parade marches down the Champs-Élysées from here.
The Tour de France has finished on the Champs-Élysées almost every year since 1975.
Champs-Élysées means the Elysian Fields, the resting place of heroes in Greek myth.
Every twenty-first of June, the Fête de la Musique fills the streets of Paris with free music, from dusk till late.
The obelisk at Concorde is more than three thousand years old. It came from Luxor in the 1830s.
During the Revolution, Place de la Concorde was where the guillotine stood.
At the Paris Olympics in 2024, Place de la Concorde became an open-air arena for skateboarding, BMX and breaking.
The Louvre began as a fortress around 1190. It became a museum in 1793.
The glass pyramid at the Louvre opened in 1989, designed by the architect I M Pei.
The Louvre is the most visited museum in the world.
The Da Vinci Code was filmed inside the Louvre in 2005, at night, after the visitors had gone.
During the 2024 Olympics, the cauldron was a glowing balloon that rose over the Tuileries garden, beside the Louvre, every evening.
In 2021 the Louvre put its whole collection online, nearly half a million works, free for anyone to browse.
Notre-Dame was begun in 1163. It reopened in December 2024, after the fire of 2019.
All road distances in France are measured from a small bronze point zero in front of Notre-Dame.
Victor Hugo's novel about Notre-Dame stirred so much feeling that the cathedral was restored in the 1800s.
Years before the fire, an art historian laser-scanned Notre-Dame, a billion points of it. Those scans helped the builders put it back together.
The Musée d'Orsay was a railway station, built for the World's Fair of 1900.
The great clocks of the old station still look out over the Seine from the Musée d'Orsay.
Orsay holds one of the world's great collections of Impressionist paintings.
In the summer of 2025, Parisians could swim in the Seine again, for the first time in a hundred years.
The Eiffel Tower was built for the World's Fair of 1889, and was meant to stand for only twenty years.
After dark, the Eiffel Tower sparkles with twenty thousand lights for a few minutes every hour.
In the summer heat, the Eiffel Tower can grow about fifteen centimetres taller.
Every medal at the Paris 2024 Olympics carried a small piece of original iron from the Eiffel Tower.
For the 2024 Olympics, beach volleyball was played in a stadium built right at the foot of the Eiffel Tower.
The Eiffel Tower was saved from demolition partly because it was so useful to science, as a giant radio mast and weather station.
